observations.title: Debian 13 base image installed for GNS3 QEMU template
observations.content:
**What**: Unattended (preseed) install of debian-live-13.7.0-amd64-standard.iso into ~/GNS3/images/QEMU/Debian-hda.qcow2 (16G, IDE /dev/sda), used by the existing GNS3 QEMU template "Debian" (linked clone, e1000, telnet console, 1024MB). Verified by booting: serial login works, interfaces named eth0/eth1 (net.ifnames=0), ssh active. Credentials root/debian and debian/debian (sudo). Extra packages: openssh-server sudo nftables tcpdump vlan curl traceroute dnsutils net-tools vim. /etc/network/interfaces only has lo. Updated images row (size/md5) in ~/.config/GNS3/3.1/gns3_controller.db.
**Why**: User needs Debian nodes in GNS3 for the p2redes practice (topology in ~/Documents/p2redes/topologia-base.md).
**Where**: ~/GNS3/images/QEMU/Debian-hda.qcow2
**Learned**: Live ISO has d-i at install/vmlinuz + install/initrd.gz; append a gzip'd cpio with preseed.cfg to the initrd and boot with -kernel/-initrd. Multi-command late_command with nested quotes failed finish-install (dropped to main menu); putting the steps in a script inside the initrd and running `chroot /target sh script || true` worked. `pkill -f <pattern>` kills the calling shell if the pattern is in its own command line.

observations.title: Session summary: p2redes
observations.content:
## Goal
Install Debian 13 from the user's live ISO so it can be used as a QEMU node in GNS3 for the p2redes networking practice.

## Instructions
Replies in Spanish, short.

## Discoveries
- GNS3 3.1.0a4 template "Debian" already existed pointing to an empty Debian-hda.qcow2 (linked clone, IDE, e1000, telnet console).
- Live ISO d-i lives in install/vmlinuz + install/initrd.gz; preseed can be appended to the initrd as an extra gzip'd cpio.
- Complex quoted late_command broke finish-install; a script in the initrd run via chroot works.

## Next Steps

observations.title: p2redes: plan de direccionamiento propuesto (topología completa)
observations.content:
**What**: Proposed full addressing for XelajuNetwork. Chain: ISP1/ISP2 -> R-EDGE -> FW -> PROXY -> R2 -> VLANs; DMZ/VPN hangs off FW.
P2P /30: 10.10.0.0/30 R-EDGE(.1)-FW(.2); 10.10.0.4/30 FW(.5)-PROXY(.6); 10.10.0.8/30 PROXY(.9)-R2(.10).
DMZ 10.10.50.0/28: FW .1, VPN-SRV .2, WEB01 .10, WEB02 .11. wg0 on VPN-SRV: 10.200.10.1/24 + 10.200.20.1/24.
VLANs on R2 eth1 subifs (gw .1): 10 admins 10.10.10.0/27, 20 users 10.10.20.0/25 (DHCP-SRV .2, reservations from .10), 30 zabbix 10.10.30.0/28 (Zabbix .2), 40 servers 10.10.40.0/27.
WAN addresses are placeholders (depend on real ISP networks).
Physical NICs: R-EDGE 3, FW 3, PROXY 2, R2 2, VPN-SRV 1, WEB01 1.
**Why**: User asked to complete addressing, routing table and security matrix starting from 10.10.0.0/16 with R-EDGE and R2 names.
**Learned**: FW uses specific routes (not a /16 summary) toward PROXY to avoid routing loops with defaults; no NAT on VPN-SRV so FW sees 10.200.x sources; VPN and DMZ share one FW interface (hairpin for Flujo B).

observations.title: p2redes: guía de configuraciones y decisiones de diseño
observations.content:
**What**: Wrote configuraciones.md (per-student config guide), alongside direccionamiento.md and prompt-topologia-figma.md. All docs in Spanish.
**Why**: User asked for all configs per component plus where each runs.
**Where**: ~/Documents/p2redes/configuraciones.md
**Learned**: Key design decisions: (1) Squid uses TPROXY (not REDIRECT) so client source IP survives to FW and R-EDGE, which solves the enunciado's "tráfico del Proxy" requirement for per-IP Multi-WAN policies; HTTPS filtered by SNI with ssl_bump peek/terminate/splice (squid-openssl), no decryption. (2) SW1 is a Debian VM with Linux bridge vlan_filtering (console-only requirement), eth7 is SPAN via tc mirred. (3) Multi-WAN: nft marks from politicas.conf -> ip rule -> tables 101/102, multipath default for balance, monitor script with marked pings (0x11/0x12) for failover. (4) WEB01 needs routes to 10.200.x via VPN-SRV because VPN and DMZ share a segment. (5) FW logs via rsyslog to /var/log/firewall root:adm 640. NOTHING HAS BEEN EXECUTED/TESTED; items marked "Verificar" (Zabbix Debian package paths, ngrok apt repo, squid options, ISP independence in GNS3 NAT/Cloud nodes).

observations.title: Session summary: p2redes
observations.content:
## Goal
Help the user plan and document the Redes 2 final project (XelajuNetwork, 5 students) in ~/Documents/p2redes.

## Instructions
Replies in Spanish, short. Project documents are written in Spanish. User's router names: R-EDGE (Multi-WAN) and R2 (internal). Base network 10.10.0.0/16.

## Discoveries
- Flujo B path: client -> ISP -> R-EDGE (DNAT UDP 51820) -> FW -> VPN-SRV -> FW -> PROXY (routing hop) -> R2 -> VLAN; no NAT on VPN-SRV.
- VPN and DMZ share 10.10.50.0/28 on one FW interface, so WEB01 needs routes to 10.200.x via VPN-SRV.
- Squid must use TPROXY to keep client source IP for FW and Multi-WAN per-IP policies.
- CGNAT on ISPs may prevent real remote VPN access; client may need to sit on the WAN-side network.

## Accomplished
- ✅ Read Enunciado.pdf (16 pages) and explained Flujo B.
- ✅ direccionamiento.md: addressing, routes, security matrix.
- ✅ prompt-topologia-figma.md: prompt for an AI to draw the topology in Figma.
- ✅ configuraciones.md: per-student configs, environment table, tests, troubleshooting.
- 🔲 Nothing executed or tested in GNS3 yet.

## Next Steps
- Build in GNS3 following the order in configuraciones.md section 2.3 and fix what fails.
- Replace ISP placeholder addresses with real ones.
- Check the items marked "Verificar".

## Relevant Files
- ~/Documents/p2redes/Enunciado.pdf — project statement
- ~/Documents/p2redes/direccionamiento.md — source of truth for addressing
- ~/Documents/p2redes/configuraciones.md — config guide
- ~/Documents/p2redes/prompt-topologia-figma.md — Figma prompt

observations.title: p2redes: review of teammates' proxy.md and VPN summary
observations.content:
**What**: Reviewed ~/Documents/redes/proxy.md (student 2) and resumen_vpn_y_remotos.md (student 4) against the repo docs (2026-10-04). Read-only review, repo docs not changed yet.
**Why**: User asked whether both are coherent and correct.
**Where**: ~/Documents/redes/ (outside the repo)
**Learned**: Proxy: addressing/routes/ACL nets/portal 8080 match our plan. Problems: (1) asks R2 to redirect TCP 80 to 10.10.0.9:3129 — remote DNAT breaks Squid intercept (original dst lost); PROXY is inline so the REDIRECT must be on PROXY itself; (2) no HTTPS handling, so HTTPS domains (facebook.com, ilovepdf.com from the statement) are neither blocked nor logged; (3) plain intercept makes web traffic leave with source 10.10.0.6, so FW needs a rule for it and Multi-WAN per-IP policies for port 80 stop working, unlike our TPROXY design; PROXY is a physical machine with NetworkManager (enp0s31f6, enx9c69d3101d16).
VPN: single wg0, no NAT, /32 per peer are fine. Uses 10.200.10.0/28 and 10.200.20.0/27 with peers from .2, differing from our /24 and .10+. Main bug: client AllowedIPs only list the VPN subnet, so clients cannot reach any VLAN. Endpoint is temporary (libvirt 192.168.122.198 via /etc/hosts alias vpn-multiwan). DMZ web server and ngrok not covered.

observations.title: p2redes: final validated review of the config guide (container tests)
observations.content:
**What**: Final review of configuraciones.md (2026-10-04), commit 2917a0f on main. Validated in debian:trixie Docker containers: nft -c for R2/FW/PROXY rulesets, squid -k parse (squid-openssl 6.13), dhcpd -t with generated reservations, suricata -T with local rules, sw1-ovs.sh against ovsdb, wg-add-peer.sh + wg-quick strip, mwan-apply.sh and failover state changes with dummy interfaces, and an end-to-end TPROXY + SNI test in network namespaces against real sites.
**Why**: User said the team is ready to run the configurations and asked to make sure they are right.
**Where**: ~/Documents/p2redes/configuraciones.md, direccionamiento.md; test harness lived in the session scratchpad (not kept).
**Learned**: (1) Squid ssl_bump peek+splice in intercept mode rejects (409, "Host header forgery") when client and Squid resolve different IPs: ~10% of allowed HTTPS failed with both on 8.8.8.8; 0 failures with a dnsmasq cache on PROXY (listen 127.0.0.1 + 10.10.0.9, min-cache-ttl=300) used by clients and Squid (dns_nameservers 127.0.0.1). (2) `ping -m` rejects hex marks; use decimal 17/18. (3) nft tproxy fails open: if Squid is down, web traffic is forwarded unfiltered. (4) Per-ISP routing tables need the connected WAN subnet or replies to on-link WAN hosts (PC-REMOTO) go to the phone gateway. (5) Debian 13 ships zabbix 7.0.22: schema at /usr/share/zabbix-server-mysql/{schema,images,data}.sql.gz, Apache conf /etc/apache2/conf-available/zabbix-frontend-php.conf; suricata default-rule-path is /var/lib/suricata/rules. (6) Squid logs two lines per spliced HTTPS connection (NONE_NONE/000 then TCP_TUNNEL/200). Not tested: physical links, phones, full multi-machine path, ngrok install, real WireGuard traffic, OVS datapath.
